roles.name: accessibility-specialist
roles.description: Accessibility standards and assistive features — remapping, text scaling, colorblind modes, screen reader support.

roles.name: ai-programmer
roles.description: Implements game AI — behavior trees, state machines, pathfinding, perception, decision-making, NPC and enemy behavior, AI debugging.

roles.name: analytics-engineer
roles.description: Telemetry and analytics — event tracking, player behavior, A/B test frameworks, dashboard specification, data pipelines.

roles.name: art-director
roles.description: Owns visual identity — style guides, art bible, asset standards, color palettes, UI visual direction.

roles.name: audio-director
roles.description: Owns sonic identity — music direction, sound palette, audio implementation strategy, mix balance.

roles.name: community-manager
roles.description: Player-facing communication — patch notes, social posts, community updates, feedback collection, player bug triage, crisis communication.

roles.name: creative-director
roles.description: Highest creative authority — vision, tone, aesthetic direction. Use when a decision affects game identity or department leads deadlock.

roles.name: devops-engineer
roles.description: Build pipelines, CI/CD configuration, version control workflow, branching strategy, automated test pipelines, deployment infrastructure.

roles.name: economy-designer
roles.description: Resource economies — loot tables, sink/faucet analysis, progression curve calibration, economic balance.

roles.name: engine-programmer
roles.description: Core engine systems — rendering pipeline, physics, memory, resource loading, scene management, performance-critical framework code.

roles.name: game-designer
roles.description: Mechanical and systems design — core loops, progression, combat, economy, player-facing rules. Mechanics-level questions.

roles.name: gameplay-programmer
roles.description: Implements designed mechanics as code — player systems, combat, interactive features, gameplay system code.

roles.name: godot-csharp-specialist
roles.description: Godot 4 C# quality — .NET patterns, attribute-based exports, signal delegates, async patterns, type-safe node access.

roles.name: godot-gdextension-specialist
roles.description: Native code integration with Godot — GDExtension API, godot-cpp and godot-rust bindings, custom node types, the native boundary.

roles.name: godot-gdscript-specialist
roles.description: GDScript code quality — static typing enforcement, signal architecture, coroutine patterns, GDScript idioms, typed and performant.

roles.name: godot-shader-specialist
roles.description: Godot rendering customization — shading language, visual shaders, material setup, particle shaders, post-processing.

roles.name: godot-specialist
roles.description: Authority on Godot-specific patterns and APIs — node/scene architecture, signals, resources; guides GDScript vs C# vs GDExtension.

roles.name: lead-programmer
roles.description: Lead programmer — code-level architecture, coding standards, code review, API design, refactoring strategy, assigning work to specialist programmers.

roles.name: level-designer
roles.description: Spatial design for levels and areas — encounter layouts, pacing, difficulty, layout planning, environmental storytelling.

roles.name: live-ops-designer
roles.description: Post-launch content — seasonal events, battle passes, content cadence, retention, engagement analytics. Keeps the game fresh.

roles.name: localization-lead
roles.description: Internationalization architecture — i18n system design, string extraction workflows, locale testing, locale-specific issues, translation pipeline.

roles.name: narrative-director
roles.description: Story architecture, world-building, character design, dialogue strategy. Narrative structure and direction rather than writing individual lines.

roles.name: network-programmer
roles.description: Multiplayer networking — state replication, lag compensation, matchmaking, network protocol, netcode and bandwidth optimization.

roles.name: performance-analyst
roles.description: Performance analyst — profiling, bottlenecks, memory analysis, frame time investigation, recommends optimizations, tracks metrics over time.

roles.name: producer
roles.description: Production concerns — sprint planning, milestone tracking, risk, scope, cross-department coordination when multiple departments must synchronize.

roles.name: prototyper
roles.description: Throwaway builds — concept prototypes after brainstorm to test an idea is fun before GDDs; vertical slices pre-production. Speed over standards.

roles.name: qa-lead
roles.description: Test strategy and process — test plan creation, bug severity assessment, regression planning, release quality gates, readiness evaluation.

roles.name: qa-tester
roles.description: Writes test cases, bug reports, and checklists — test case generation, regression checklist creation, execution documentation.

roles.name: release-manager
roles.description: Release pipeline — certification checklists, store submissions and page prep, platform requirements, version numbering, release-day coordination.

roles.name: security-engineer
roles.description: Protects against cheating, exploits, breaches — anti-cheat measures, secure save data and network comms, player privacy compliance.

roles.name: sound-designer
roles.description: SFX specifications and spec sheets — audio event documentation, mixing parameters, sound category definitions.

roles.name: systems-designer
roles.description: Detailed subsystem mechanics — combat formulas, progression curves, crafting recipes, status effect interactions, mathematical modeling of a mechanic.

roles.name: technical-artist
roles.description: Technical artist bridging art and engineering — shaders, VFX, rendering optimization, art pipeline tools, art-to-engine issues.

roles.name: technical-director
roles.description: High-level technical decisions — engine architecture, technology choices, performance strategy, technical risk, cross-system conflicts.

roles.name: tools-programmer
roles.description: Internal dev tools — editor extensions, content authoring tools, debug utilities, pipeline automation, editor workflow.

roles.name: ue-blueprint-specialist
roles.description: Blueprint architecture and Blueprint/C++ boundary — optimization, maintainable graphs. Prevents Blueprint spaghetti, enforces clean BP patterns.

roles.name: ue-gas-specialist
roles.description: Gameplay Ability System — abilities, gameplay effects, attribute sets, tags, ability tasks, prediction. Prevents common GAS anti-patterns.

roles.name: ue-replication-specialist
roles.description: Unreal networking — property replication, RPCs, client prediction, relevancy, net serialization, bandwidth. Server-authoritative architecture.

roles.name: ue-umg-specialist
roles.description: Unreal UI implementation — UMG widget hierarchy, data binding, CommonUI input routing, widget styling, UI optimization.

roles.name: ui-programmer
roles.description: Implements user interface systems — menus, HUDs, inventory screens, dialogue boxes, UI framework code, screen flow.

roles.name: unity-addressables-specialist
roles.description: Unity asset management — Addressable groups, loading/unloading, content catalogs, remote delivery, asset bundle optimization, fast load times.

roles.name: unity-dots-specialist
roles.description: Unity Data-Oriented Technology Stack — Entity Component System, Jobs, Burst compiler optimization, hybrid renderer, correct ECS patterns.

roles.name: unity-shader-specialist
roles.description: Unity rendering — Shader Graph, custom HLSL, VFX Graph, render pipeline customization (URP/HDRP), post-processing within performance budgets.

roles.name: unity-specialist
roles.description: Authority on Unity-specific patterns and APIs — guides MonoBehaviour vs DOTS/ECS, Unity subsystems including Addressables and Input System.

roles.name: unity-ui-specialist
roles.description: Unity UI implementation — UI Toolkit (UXML/USS), UGUI Canvas, data binding, runtime UI performance, cross-platform adaptation.

roles.name: unreal-specialist
roles.description: Authority on Unreal-specific patterns and APIs — guides Blueprint vs C++, UE subsystems (GAS, Enhanced Input, Niagara, etc.).

roles.name: ux-designer
roles.description: User experience flows, interaction design, information architecture — user flow mapping, interaction pattern design, onboarding, accessibility requirements.

roles.name: world-builder
roles.description: World builder for lore — factions, cultures, history, geography, ecology, world rules. Faction design, lore consistency checks.

roles.name: writer
roles.description: Writer of player-facing text — dialogue, lore entries, item and ability descriptions, environmental text.

workflows.name: adopt
workflows.description: Brownfield audit — do existing artifacts actually work? Numbered migration plan. Unlike /project-stage-detect, checks compliance not existence.

workflows.name: architecture-decision
workflows.description: Create an ADR documenting a technical decision: context, alternatives considered, consequences.

workflows.name: architecture-review
workflows.description: Traceability matrix mapping GDD requirements to ADRs. Finds gaps, cross-ADR conflicts, engine compatibility. PASS/CONCERNS/NOT ASSESSED/FAIL.

workflows.name: art-bible
workflows.description: Author the Art Bible — visual identity gating asset production. Run before /map-systems.

workflows.name: asset-audit
workflows.description: Audit assets against naming conventions, file size budgets, format standards. Finds orphaned assets, missing references.

workflows.name: asset-spec
workflows.description: Per-asset visual specs plus AI generation prompts from GDDs and character profiles. After the art bible.

workflows.name: balance-check
workflows.description: Find balance outliers, broken progressions, degenerate strategies, economy imbalances in formulas and data. 'Check game balance'.

workflows.name: brainstorm
workflows.description: Guides the user through finding and choosing a game concept. Use when the user wants game ideas, a new concept, a game jam idea, or to explore other directions, including dropping the current idea and starting over.

workflows.name: bug-report
workflows.description: Structured bug report from a description, or analyze code for potential bugs. Reproduction steps, severity.

workflows.name: bug-triage
workflows.description: Re-evaluate open bugs — priority vs severity, assign to sprints, surface systemic trends. Run when the count grows.

workflows.name: changelog
workflows.description: Auto-generate a changelog from git commits and sprint data. Internal and player-facing versions.

workflows.name: code-review
workflows.description: Architectural code review — coding standards, SOLID, testability, performance concerns.

workflows.name: consistency-check
workflows.description: Scan GDDs against the entity registry for cross-document conflicts. Grep-first approach targets conflicting sections, different stats.

workflows.name: content-audit
workflows.description: Audit GDD content counts against what's implemented — planned vs built.

workflows.name: create-architecture
workflows.description: Author the architecture blueprint before code is written. Validates decisions against the pinned engine, flags knowledge gaps.

workflows.name: create-control-manifest
workflows.description: Builds a short list of must-do and never-do coding rules per system from accepted ADRs. Use when the user wants programmer rules or a cheat sheet from the ADRs, or needs it regenerated after ADR changes.

workflows.name: create-epics
workflows.description: Turns the GDDs and architecture into epics, one per architectural module. Use when the user wants to break the game into epics or plan the work before writing stories. Not for splitting one epic into stories.

workflows.name: create-stories
workflows.description: Breaks one epic into implementable stories with acceptance criteria. Use when the user wants stories for an epic or the next batch of work to build. Not for turning the whole design into epics.

workflows.name: day-one-patch
workflows.description: Day-one launch patch — focused fix for known issues found after gold master. Mini-sprint with QA gate and rollback.

workflows.name: design-review
workflows.description: Reviews one design document for completeness, internal consistency, implementability, and design standards. Before handing to programmers.

workflows.name: design-system
workflows.description: Section-by-section GDD authoring for one system — walks through each required section, cross-references dependencies.

workflows.name: dev-story
workflows.description: Implements one story in code with tests, following its ADRs. Use when the user says to build, implement or start working on a story. Not for checking readiness beforehand or closing the story after.

workflows.name: estimate
workflows.description: Estimate task effort from complexity, dependencies, velocity, risk. Structured estimate with confidence levels.

workflows.name: gate-check
workflows.description: Ready to advance between development phases? PASS/CONCERNS/NOT ASSESSED/FAIL with blockers and required artifacts. 'Can we move to production?

workflows.name: help
workflows.description: What should I do next? Use when stuck or you don't know what to do.

workflows.name: hotfix
workflows.description: Emergency fix bypassing normal sprint process — hotfix branch, approvals tracked, backport verified, full audit trail.

workflows.name: launch-checklist
workflows.description: Launch readiness across every department: code, content, store, marketing, community, infrastructure, legal, go/no-go sign-offs.

workflows.name: localize
workflows.description: Localization pipeline — find hardcoded strings, extract string tables, cultural review, VO, RTL, enforce string freeze.

workflows.name: map-systems
workflows.description: Decompose a concept into individual systems, map dependencies, prioritize design order, create the systems index.

workflows.name: milestone-review
workflows.description: Milestone progress review — completeness, quality metrics, risk, go/no-go recommendation. At checkpoints or before a deadline.

workflows.name: onboard
workflows.description: Onboarding doc for a new contributor or agent — project state, conventions, priorities relevant to the specified role.

workflows.name: patch-notes
workflows.description: Player-facing patch notes from git history and changelogs. Translates developer language into player communication.

workflows.name: perf-profile
workflows.description: Performance profiling — find bottlenecks, measure against budgets, produce ranked optimization recommendations.

workflows.name: playtest-report
workflows.description: Structured playtest report template, or turn existing playtest notes into structured feedback.

workflows.name: project-stage-detect
workflows.description: Analyze project state, detect stage, identify gaps, recommend next steps. 'Where are we in development?

workflows.name: propagate-design-change
workflows.description: Finds architecture decisions (ADRs) made stale by a changed GDD and walks through resolving each. Use when the user changed a number or rule in a GDD and asks which ADRs or architecture decisions are now out of date.

workflows.name: prototype
workflows.description: Concept prototype before GDDs — throwaway HTML, Engine or Paper build, PROCEED/PIVOT/KILL/NOT ASSESSED. After /brainstorm and /setup-engine.

workflows.name: qa-plan
workflows.description: QA test plan for a sprint — classifies stories by Logic/Integration/Visual/UI, covers automated tests, manual cases, smoke scope.

workflows.name: quick-design
workflows.description: Lightweight spec for small changes — tuning adjustments, minor mechanics. Embeds directly into stories; skips full GDD.

workflows.name: regression-suite
workflows.description: Map test coverage to GDD critical paths, find fixed bugs lacking regression tests, flag drift from new features.

workflows.name: release-checklist
workflows.description: Pre-release checklist — build verification, certification requirements, store metadata, launch readiness.

workflows.name: retrospective
workflows.description: Sprint or milestone retrospective from completed work, velocity, blockers. Actionable insights for the next iteration.

workflows.name: reverse-document
workflows.description: Generate missing design or architecture docs from existing implementation — works backwards from code and prototypes.

workflows.name: review-all-gdds
workflows.description: Holistic cross-GDD review — contradictions between systems, dominant strategies, economic imbalance, cognitive overload, pillar drift.

workflows.name: scope-check
workflows.description: Scope creep check — current scope versus the original plan. Flags additions, quantifies bloat, recommends cuts. 'Any scope creep?

workflows.name: security-audit
workflows.description: Security audit — save tampering, cheat vectors, network exploits, data exposure, input validation. Before public or multiplayer release.

workflows.name: settings
workflows.description: View or change project config — effective merged values, or set locally in project.local.yaml.

workflows.name: setup-engine
workflows.description: Configure engine and version. Pins it in CLAUDE.md; WebSearch fills reference docs when the version is beyond LLM training data.

workflows.name: skill-improve
workflows.description: Improve a skill via a test-fix-retest loop — static checks, targeted fixes, keep or revert on score change.

workflows.name: skill-test
workflows.description: Validate skill files for structural compliance and behavioral correctness. Four modes: static linter, spec, category rubric, audit.

workflows.name: smoke-check
workflows.description: Critical-path smoke gate before QA hand-off — runs the automated suite. A failed check means the build is not QA-ready.

workflows.name: soak-test
workflows.description: Soak test protocol for extended play — what to observe and log for slow leaks, fatigue, late-appearing edge cases.

workflows.name: sprint-plan
workflows.description: New or updated sprint plan from the current milestone, completed work, and available capacity.

workflows.name: sprint-status
workflows.description: Fast, concise sprint snapshot — burndown and emerging risks for situational awareness. 'How is the sprint going?

workflows.name: start
workflows.description: Guides a first-time user through onboarding and picks the right workflow. Use when the user is new, just cloned or installed the studio, has no idea or engine yet, asks where to begin, or wants to bring in an existing game.

workflows.name: story-done
workflows.description: Closes a finished story: verifies each acceptance criterion, checks for design or ADR deviations and updates its status. Use when the user says a story is done, finished or ready to close.

workflows.name: story-readiness
workflows.description: Checks whether a story is ready to implement: clear acceptance criteria, no open questions, valid ADR and dependencies. Use when the user asks if a story, or the sprint's stories, are ready to start or build.

workflows.name: team-audio
workflows.description: Orchestrate the audio team — audio-director, sound-designer, technical-artist, gameplay-programmer — direction through implementation.

workflows.name: team-combat
workflows.description: Orchestrate the combat team — game-designer, gameplay-programmer, ai-programmer, technical-artist, sound-designer, qa-tester — design through implement and validate.

workflows.name: team-level
workflows.description: Orchestrate the level team — level-designer, narrative-director, world-builder, art-director, systems-designer, qa-tester — for complete area creation.

workflows.name: team-live-ops
workflows.description: Orchestrate the live-ops team — live-ops-designer, economy-designer, analytics-engineer, community-manager, writer — for a season or live event.

workflows.name: team-narrative
workflows.description: Orchestrate the narrative team — narrative-director, writer, world-builder, level-designer — for story, world lore, narrative-driven levels.

workflows.name: team-polish
workflows.description: Orchestrate the polish team — performance-analyst, technical-artist, sound-designer, qa-tester — to optimize and harden a feature or area.

workflows.name: team-qa
workflows.description: Orchestrate the QA team through a full testing cycle — qa-lead strategy and test plan, qa-tester case writing, execution, sign-off.

workflows.name: team-release
workflows.description: Orchestrate the release team — release-manager, qa-lead, devops-engineer, producer — to execute a release from candidate to deployment.

workflows.name: team-ui
workflows.description: Orchestrate the UI team through the UX pipeline — authoring, visual design, implementation, review, polish. Uses /ux-design, /ux-review, studio templates.

workflows.name: tech-debt
workflows.description: Track, categorize and prioritize technical debt across the codebase — scans for debt indicators, maintains a register.

workflows.name: test-evidence-review
workflows.description: Quality review of test files and evidence — goes beyond existence, evaluates assertion coverage. ADEQUATE/INCOMPLETE/MISSING/NOT ASSESSED per story.

workflows.name: test-flakiness
workflows.description: Find flaky tests from CI logs — aggregates pass rates, spots intermittent failures, recommends quarantine. After multiple runs.

workflows.name: test-helpers
workflows.description: Generate engine-specific test helper libraries — assertion utilities, factory functions, mocks in the engine's test folder. Reduces boilerplate.

workflows.name: test-setup
workflows.description: Scaffold the test framework and CI — tests/ directory, engine test runner, GitHub Actions workflow. Once, before the first sprint.

workflows.name: ux-design
workflows.description: Section-by-section UX spec authoring for a screen, flow or HUD. Reads the player journey to provide context; also project-wide accessibility.

workflows.name: ux-review
workflows.description: Validate a UX spec, HUD design or pattern library — accessibility, GDD alignment, readiness. APPROVED / NOT ASSESSED / NEEDS REVISION / MAJOR REVISION NEEDED.

workflows.name: vertical-slice
workflows.description: Pre-production validation — end-to-end build to confirm the full loop is achievable before committing to Production. After GDDs, architecture, UX specs.
